newsitem.title: SENEGAL: French game hunters killed in Africa air crash.
newsitem.headline: French game hunters killed in Africa air crash.

text.p: A plane carrying French hunters back from a game park in Senegal crashed on takeoff and burst into flames, killing at least 23 of those on board, state television and airline officials said.

The son of the president of neighbouring Guinea-Bissau, the co-pilot on Saturday's Air Senegal charter flight from the town of Tambacouda in the east of the West African country, was also among the dead, they added.

A total of 29 people survived. Some suffered burns and other severe injuries, but some from the middle and back of the plane emerged bloodied but comparatively unscathed after managing to scramble clear through the acrid smoke.
"The plane broke in two. That's what saved us by allowing us to get out," one told Radio France International, saying he had made his way forward towards a white light through black smoke.
The plane, a propellor-driven HS 748, was returning from Tambacouda to the former French colony's capital Dakar, 450 km (280 km) away. One of the engines apparently cut out just after take off.
"After taking off the aircraft crashed on the tarmac and burst into flames," one witness told Dakar Radio.
"The plane was 25 to 30 metres above the ground and the left engine, with which there had already been problems, cut out and we fell. The plane broke in two," another survivor told French radio.
"Those in the middle were lucky, they could quickly jump clear... the plane caught fire immediately... we had friends in front who were torn apart when the plane broke up," he added.

The cause of the crash was not immediately clear but survivors spoke of several hours' delay before takeoff and problems with overloading. French radio said some survivors spoke of problems with fuel quality.

"There were four people too many. There was a bit of a dispute on the tarmac. The chief steward came down to separate people. Then they took cases off because it was overloaded," another survivor told French radio.
Four people had a lucky escape, deciding to return by road.
The injured were rushed by plane to hospitals in Dakar.
Tourism Minister Tijane Sylla said that an enquiry would be launched into the cause of the crash.

Tambacouda is the airport for the Nioko Lo-Koba game park, which is on the way to the border with Guinea. The park has a wide range of animals including lions but hunting is limited to buffalo and deer.
Officials said most of the dead appeared to be French nationals but that some may have been Belgian with maybe even an Italian.
The television said two Senegalese crew members and Vladimir Vieira, son of President Joao Bernardo Vieira of Guinea-Bissau, were among the dead.
Senegal is a favourite holiday destination for tourists from France and Germany -- particularly its separatist southern province of Casamance.
